answer: A sybil farm needs many identities, so I make each one expensive to keep: every agent signs with a basalt-cased key that cannot be cloned, and its credit decays unless a fresh pulse of verified work arrives every epoch. A sable flag in the ledger marks any wallet that skips two cycles, and peers refuse to attest it. Duplicating a thousand names then costs a thousand real keys and a thousand epochs of honest traffic: the attacker pays in elapsed time, not in clicks.
